summary: In run_self_improve_loop() (line 281), admitted_skills is built as list(skill_library['active_skills'].keys()) — ID strings only. Line 284 passes this ID-only list into _SKILL_PROPOSAL_PROMPT. But _admit_skill_to_library() (lines 583-590) stores description, expected_effects, and capability_gap_addressed for every admitted skill. Those fields are available in skill_library at prompt-build time but are silently dropped. The LLM therefore cannot detect semantic duplicates: a new proposal 'inference_limiter_v1 — halt inference when token ceiling reached' passes the ID dedup check (line 331) and all scoring gates even if 'token_budget_manager_v1 — tracks token budget per inference call and halts when limit exceeded' is already admitted. Only the ID is checked; capability semantics are invisible to the model.
evidence: line 281: admitted_skills = list(skill_library.get('active_skills', {}).keys()) — .keys() strips all non-ID fields
line 284: admitted_skills=json.dumps(admitted_skills, sort_keys=True) — JSON array of bare IDs injected into prompt
lines 583-590: _admit_skill_to_library stores description, expected_effects, capability_gap_addressed — all present in skill_library at cycle start
live probe: after admitting token_budget_manager_v1 with full proposal, admitted_ids=['helen_autoresearch_v1','token_budget_manager_v1']; description and gap silently dropped from prompt context
line 331: dedup check is skill_id in skill_library['active_skills'] — exact ID only, no semantic comparison
no existing test validates that descriptions appear in the built prompt
hypothesis: If admitted_skills context includes description and capability_gap_addressed (not just IDs), the LLM can avoid proposing skills that duplicate admitted capabilities under a new name, reducing semantic-duplicate cycles and wasted gate passes.

Line 284 stays unchanged (json.dumps still works on dict). Proposal only — operator must apply.
